entry.title: Zombie Apartment Survival: Day 1 to Day 401 (Full Movie)

media:group.media:title: Zombie Apartment Survival: Day 1 to Day 401 (Full Movie)
media:group.media:description:
Zombie Apartment Survival: 401 Days (Full Movie) — the complete trilogy in one video.
Trapped on the 12th floor of Harbor Court Tower in Chicago. No bunker, no plan, no bag by the door — just 60 gallons of water, 21 days of food, and two rules written on the inside of the front door: quiet is armor, count everything. Below him, in flat 11B, an old freighter engineer named Teodor answers in cardboard signs and a rope basket. Next door, in 12C, Mr. Harlan is still in there — and he has not stopped. A year of stretching water, sprouted lentils, and a 20-pound propane tank carried across a balcony partition 12 floors up. Then, on Day 365, at 5:47 in the morning, the elevator bell rings — in a building with no power.
The doors slide open on light. Three people in gray coveralls stand in the car, felt booties on their shoes, and a slate in white chalk letters: WE SAW YOUR LIGHT. DAY 230. Seven people have been alive above him all year, on floor 24, growing lettuce, spinach and tomatoes under purple lights — kept alive by a diesel generator with 300 gallons of fuel and a problem Teodor spots in one touch: diesel bug. And at noon every day, a voice on the shortwave says the same thing: the harbor ferry Kestrel, Pier Two, final muster May 6th. Twenty-nine days. The plan: elevator to the basement, loading dock, alley, pier — while Desmond makes the noise that holds the whole avenue.
Day 400. The last meal. The seed tin. Barrel fires on the avenue, 1,100 feet north. Day 401, May 6, 41 degrees. At 4:50 in the morning, nine people climb to the roof. A generator on a pallet, 200 feet of rope, four car horns — noise for 40 minutes while nine people cross 1,400 feet of rooftops to Pier Two. Desmond says it out loud: 40 minutes. Not 41. At 5:10, in a 90-foot corridor, the maintenance man is still there. At 5:31, the alley. At 5:48, the rooftops. And at 18 minutes, the horns falter. The ferry leaves at 6. Six o'clock. Everybody aboard.

entry.title: How to Survive When It Rains for 1 Year on a Farm

media:group.media:title: How to Survive When It Rains for 1 Year on a Farm
media:group.media:description:
How to Survive 1 Year of Rain on a Farm — a survival story from Stick Survival Log.
A storm has settled over the valley and it isn't going anywhere. The lane home is underwater, a truck is already floating off the road, and the only way up is a line of fence posts climbing the slope. Forty posts stand between the road and the house, and the flood is swallowing them one at a time. The rain is here to stay for twelve months.

media:group.media:title: Zombie Survival Billionaire's Bunker 1 Year
media:group.media:description:
Zombie Outbreak: 1 Year Trapped in Rowan Pike's Bunker.
You pull up to a gated estate in your pool-service van on the first morning of the outbreak. The job on the dash is a heater repair in the lower level, and it needs a signature. Nobody answers the gate, so you lean on the visitor button. A brass bell answers from the gatehouse roof, and the first dead thing you meet is dressed for dinner, still holding its tray. Three rings, and the whole lawn is looking at you.
Past the steel door at the end of the service ramp is the Residence, a bunker dressed up as a five-star hotel: marble floors, a chandelier, a screen showing a garden that isn't there. Somewhere overhead, the owner's recorded voice is still running the house, welcoming guests who will never arrive and offering you everything inside.
Inside: a pool, a cinema, a sauna, a wine cellar, a garden growing under purple lights, and a generator the size of a delivery van. You came to fix a heater. You are staying for a year. And the dead outside don't hunt by sight. They hunt by sound - and this place is full of machines that hum.
If you were LOG, would you open the gate, or leave the bell silent forever? Tell me in the comments. Part 2 starts at Day 366.

media:group.media:title: Nuclear Apocalypse Survival: First 30 Days
media:group.media:description:
Nuclear Apocalypse Survival: 30 Days in the Vault - a nuclear survival story.
At 4:07 in the morning, the sirens start. You are the night maintenance worker on the 12th floor of Meridian Tower, and you came up to change one burned-out light bulb. The blast is seven and a half miles away, and you have about ten minutes before the fallout arrives. Down you go, past the broken lobby doors, to sub-level 4, where a steel door says Records Vault. Inside: a meter, a cot, and three rules on masking tape. Dirt stays at the door. Nothing burns in here. Read the meter before the door. This is thirty days after the blast, one problem at a time - water, cold, smoke, hunger, and a radio that has been dead since Day 1. Until Day 30, when a new voice speaks.

entry.title: Zombie Outbreak: Day 1 to Day 500 on the 50th Floor (Full Story)

media:group.media:title: Zombie Outbreak: Day 1 to Day 500 on the 50th Floor (Full Story)
media:group.media:description:
Zombie Outbreak: 500 Days on the 50th Floor (Full Story) - a zombie survival story.
Day 500, 5:40 a.m. You are in a window-washing cradle fifty floors up, and the plaza below is empty. To understand how a building becomes a trap, you have to start at lunch, on an ordinary Tuesday. Three people - you, the night cleaner, Dara the sous-chef, and Tomas the delivery rider - trapped in the Skyline Room on the 50th floor of Meridian Tower, while the dead below follow one thing only: sound. The generator dies. The pantry runs out at exactly 220 days. A guard climbs the stairs one step at a time and never stops. The plaza empties, and nobody knows where they went. And on Day 500, when the cradle finally moves, you understand what the tower was doing with you all along.

media:group.media:title: Zombie Shopping Mall Survival 1 Year
media:group.media:description:
Zombie Outbreak: 365 Days Trapped in a Shopping Mall - a zombie survival story.
At 2:04 a.m. every light in the mall dies at once, and the south doors begin to boom. You are the night guard, alone, holding a flashlight, a radio and a ring of keys - and forty steel gates that should drop over forty storefronts will not move without power.
The whole mall gapes open in the dark, and this place hunts by light and by sound. Your only map is the Directory board in the atrium: green means safe, grey means emptied, red means lost. Month by month the board shrinks - 31 green at dawn, 6 green at half a year, 3 green at the end - while you fight the gates, the thaw, the dark, the food cliff, the greenhouse heat, the water, the rats, the storm, the cold snap, the long dark and the ice. Then, at 3 a.m., a horn blows three short blasts from the parking garage roof. Someone spray-painted an orange arrow on the asphalt, pointing south-east. And on the final night, you aim your lantern the same way - and far across the dark, a light answers.

media:group.media:title: Zombie Cruise Ship Survival 100 Days
media:group.media:description:
Zombie Apocalypse: 100 Days on a Cruise Ship - a zombie survival story.
At 3:12 in the morning, a cheerful voice fills every corridor of the cruise ship Halcyon: "Good morning, passengers! Breakfast is served on deck seven!" The night laundry worker wakes up to footsteps overhead - and to a ship where the dead don't hunt by sight. They follow sound. Every announcement, every bell, every gong is a leash, and the passengers follow every tug.
For 100 days he uses the ship's own announcement system as a clock, as bait, and as his only weapon - from the theatre filled with a seated audience waiting for a curtain that never rises, to the fog, the other ship with two red lights, the storm that kills the engines, and the silence after the voice dies on Day 12. Day 100 brings land at last - and a voice he knows by heart.
Would you walk into the trees toward that voice? Tell me in the comments.

entry.title: 76 Days Alone on a 6-Foot Raft (True Story)

media:group.media:title: 76 Days Alone on a 6-Foot Raft (True Story)
media:group.media:description:
76 Days Adrift on a Raft - the true survival story of Steven Callahan.
The true story of Steven Callahan, who survived 76 days adrift in the Atlantic after his sloop sank in 1982. Based on his memoir, Adrift: Seventy-Six Days Lost at Sea.
A whale strike in the dark. A six-foot life raft. One knife, zero food, zero drink. From there, every single thing he owns gets converted into days of life - the Count. Learn how a solar still turns salt water into drink, how a floating raft grows its own island of fish, how a toy spear becomes the difference between eating and starving, and how a forgotten Boy Scout fork plugs a hole that nearly kills him. 76 days. About 1,800 miles. One impossible chain home: dorado drew birds, birds drew fishermen, fishermen drew him home.

media:group.media:description:
Zombie Outbreak: 7 Days Trapped in a Library - a zombie survival story.
At 6:41 a.m., a bus runs dry in front of a library, a hiss turns a hundred heads, and the only way in is a brass key taped to a clipboard. 7 days. A building that is heavy, flammable, and fragile.
Every chapter is one real survival problem: glass doors against the tide, water from the pipes, a candle fire in a paper building, a back door with no handle, a wet blueprint, and a row of bookcases that can become the loudest noise in town. Learn how to drain a building's pipes, why a fire blanket beats an extinguisher when silence matters, and how to rescue wet paper.
